document.title: Prospects for Northern Alliance Forces to Seize Kabul
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret/Noforn/X1] Compares Taliban and Northern Alliance strength around Kabul. The Taliban Kabul Central Corps has about 130 tanks and 7,000 soldiers against Fahim Khan's roughly 10,000 troops. The Alliance is unlikely to seize Kabul unaided, but Russian arms deliveries via Tajikistan may change the balance. The Alliance took Kabul on November 13, 2001.

key_claims: The Northern Alliance cannot successfully conduct a large-scale offensive to seize and hold Kabul at its present combat power.
Taliban Kabul Central Corps (~7,000 soldiers, 130 tanks) outmatches Northern Alliance (~10,000 troops, ~40 tanks) in weapons.
Winter and difficult Hindu Kush supply lines hurt the Northern Alliance more than the Taliban.
Fahim Khan is relying on coalition air strikes to weaken the Taliban and conserve his forces for post-conflict posturing.
Northern Alliance leaders reportedly shelved plans to take Kabul by force, approaching only to the city's limits.
Anti-Taliban groups disagree over how to form a post-Taliban representative government.
